transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-30
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Irwin (Vecora CTO), Leah Kim (Vecora PM), Jordan Park (Vecora ML Eng)
Links shared: demo deck (slides.redwood/demo-vc), sample schema repo (github.com/redwood/json-mode-examples), benchmark spreadsheet (sheet.redwood/vecora-bench)

Summary (auto): quick walkthrough of JSON mode + tool-calling and orchestration/fallbacks; focus on reliability and predictable output for downstream parsers; discuss Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs and initial POC scope.

00:00 Alex: hey everyone, um, thanks for joining — I think we've got, like, five people on. welcome — I'm Alex, I'm the AE on this account and with me is Priya from the SE team. we'll run through a focused demo: JSON-mode structured output, schema-enforced tool calling, and how Redwood handles orchestration and fallbacks when capacity or latency constraints happen.

00:18 Priya: hi! quick agenda — show API and Console JSON-mode, then Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization for cost, then a live scenario where we call an internal enrichment tool and fallback to a cheaper model if needed. any must-haves from Vecora?

00:32 Sam: yeah, thanks. our main things are deterministic structured responses for downstream pipelines, and guaranteed SLOs for customer-facing flows. also security — we need SOC 2 and SAML for SSO.

00:46 Leah: and overlap — our product requires tech that can guarantee the JSON shape or we have to add a ton of post-processing.

00:58 Priya: got it. we'll show the schema enforcement and the guardrails; note that JSON-mode isn't 100% like static typing, but we have validation and automatic fallback policies.

01:15 Priya: okay opening the Console — here is the request playground, select model, toggle JSON-mode schema enforcement. I'm going to paste a schema: {
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "customer_intent": {"type": "string"},
    "entities": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}}
  },
  "required": ["customer_intent"]
}

01:50 Sam: quick question — if the model deviates from schema what happens? do you do auto-correct?

02:02 Priya: good q. two things: validation fails the response and we surface a structured error back to the caller; and second, we can configure a repair step — either ask the model to reformat, or run a deterministic sanitizer in our toolchain. we also support function/tool calling where you can register a sanitizer endpoint to be called when validation fails.

02:30 Jordan: so the sanitizer would be hosted by us? or by Redwood?

02:36 Priya: both options. for Hosted API we can host a small sanitization lambda in the request path; for Private or Dedicated you can register an internal endpoint accessible via VPC.

02:50 Alex: also worth calling out Optimize suggestions — the Console will recommend batching sizes, caching TTLs, and a quantization profile if it detects mostly short sequences. that helps that predictable cost target you mentioned, Sam.

03:10 Priya: demo time: I'll run a sample call. switching to API view, this is a curl example: POST /v1/generate with body: prompt + schema_mode: "json_enforce" + schema: <attached>. sending...

03:34 (transcript noise)

03:44 System: (note: network jitter) request sent

03:50 Response: validation_error: missing required property "customer_intent"

03:56 Priya: ok so here validation failed — Console highlights the offending token ranges. I'm going to enable a fallback: first do a model re-format attempt (same model, 1 retry), then call a deterministic sanitization function that normalizes keys and types. toggling fallback policy now.

04:20 Leah: for us the re-format retry is interesting because sometimes the model returns extra commentary and we just need it stripped.

04:28 Priya: exactly — and you can configure allowed commentary fields or block them. I'm going to demo tool calling: register a tool named "entity_extractor_service" which returns canonical entities as JSON and has a 500ms SLA. we'll orchestrate: generate -> if entities confidence < 0.8 then call extractor tool -> merge result.

04:55 Alex: here is the important part — orchestration policies are first-class. you can route by latency, cost, or model tier. in our POC templates we often route mission-critical endpoints to Dedicated pools with lower tail latency, and lower-criticality ops to hosted cheaper models for cost savings.

05:18 Jordan: hypothetically if the extractor tool is down what happens?

05:24 Priya: good edge case — we support fallback chains: if tool A responds slow or errors, call tool B (e.g., a cached denormalizer), or fall back to the model-only path but mark the response provenance so downstream knows confidence is lower. we also have circuit breakers and automatic retries with exponential backoff.

05:45 Sam: is that propagated to logs/audits? our compliance team will want to see when fallbacks happened and why.

05:52 Priya: yes, Console traces show per-request route, timing, which tool was called, model hash, quantization profile, and any validation failures. all captured in the request timeline and exported to your SIEM.

06:10 (30s break in demo while Priya switches tabs)

06:40 Priya: now a live scenario: we'll simulate high load — switch routing policy to prefer cost-saving model but with an automatic fallback to Dedicated if latency > 250ms. sending a batch of 10 concurrent requests.

07:00 (demo)

07:10 Response logs: 6/10 returned from cheap-hosted-model avg 120ms; 4/10 auto-routed to Dedicated due to queueing — avg 230ms. one request hit a tool timeout and went to fallback sanitizer.

07:32 Leah: ok that's great, how do you set alerting thresholds? do you have out-of-the-box alerts for % requests hitting fallback?

07:40 Alex: yes labeled metrics include fallback rate, schema-violations, errors, p95/p99 latency per route and model. you can create alerts in Console or forward to Datadog/Prometheus.

07:56 Jordan: cost question — that auto routing to Dedicated — will that spike billing unpredictably?

08:03 Alex: two levers: Dedicated buffer capacity and burst policies. you set commitments (monthly) and burst configs; Optimize simulates expected unit costs given historical load and suggests commit sizes to stabilize unit price. we'll include those numbers in the POC pricing.

08:22 Sam: security — quick checklist: SOC 2 report, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration — yes?

08:31 Alex: yes to all. Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS; audit logs capture request headers and model version; SSO via SAML/Okta is supported; RBAC scoping per route. we'll attach our compliance packet.

08:48 Priya: small note — in Private deployments you can keep the sanitizer and tools entirely on-prem and Redwood's control plane will orchestrate via your network.

09:05 (crosstalk)

09:20 Priya: next, an example of structured tool-calling with function-like tool registration. I'll call a payment-risk-evaluator tool in the flow. sending prompt: "analyze this order and return {risk_score:int, reasons:[string] }" and register the tool to supply historical fraud flags if needed.

09:49 Response: model returns risk_score 2, reasons ["low historical risk"] — validated against schema. good.

09:58 Jordan: if model returns string for risk_score do you coerce?

10:04 Priya: we won't coerce silently. validation fails unless you configure permissive coerce rules; we recommend explicit sanitizer tool to convert types so behavior is auditable.

10:20 Sam: how about function/tool auth? we can't have arbitrary calls out to internet endpoints for PII.

10:27 Alex: tool endpoints use signed certs and mTLS; for Dedicated/Private we can restrict network paths. also you can configure per-tool RBAC so only a given route or service account can invoke it.

10:42 Leah: can we run a canary rollout for the sanitizer? want to test on 5% traffic first.

10:49 Priya: yes — rollouts are built-in. you can do canary, A/B, or staged percent rollouts by route. and automatic rollback on regression signals (schema violations or p95 latency increases).

11:10 (brief pause)

11:26 Priya: switching to Optimize tab — this is the batch/caching advisor. it analyzes token distributions and suggests: for this workflow, prefix caching + kv cache for conversation contexts, batch size 8 for p50<200ms, and int8 quant profile to cut token compute by ~3x with minor quality tradeoff.

11:52 Jordan: how do you measure quality tradeoffs? we need objective metrics.

11:58 Priya: tie Optimize to your evals — upload prompt set and metrics (exact-match, BLEU-ish, or downstream success). Optimize runs tests across quant profiles and reports regression deltas; you can set a rollback threshold.

12:20 Sam: ok good. about the POC — we want to validate the parser for 3 flows and ensure <3% schema violations and p99 < 350ms. realistic?

12:33 Alex: yes that's within POC scope. recommended POC: 2 weeks, 50k requests simulated, include one enrichment tool and both Hosted and Dedicated routing to compare. we'll propose pricing.

12:48 Leah: any gotchas on third-party model licenses? we occasionally need models with certain commercial terms.

12:56 Priya: we have a model catalog; licensing and vetted performance notes are in Console. if you need a specific open model we can discuss model onboarding and licensing.

13:10 (example error in transcript: "Redwood Dedicate" mentioned by Sam)

13:28 Priya: quick live failure injection: I'm going to flip the extractor tool to return 500s to show fallback and auditing.

13:40 Tool logs: extractor 500 x3, fallback sanitizer invoked, one request flagged with provenance "sanitized_tool_fallback".

13:55 Leah: show the audit — ok I can see the request timeline and the exact fallback reason and confidence scores. this works for compliance.

14:10 Alex: closing loop — we'll attach security docs, SOC 2, and a proposed pricing and commit for Dedicated. Priya will drop the JSON-mode quickstart and sample schema repo.

14:22 Sam: ok path looks clear. one ask: can we get an export of the Console traces in NDJSON for ingestion?

14:30 Priya: yes we support NDJSON streams and webhook forwarding.

14:38 Jordan: minor UX note: can we have Console show schema diff across model versions?

14:44 Priya: that's on roadmap; we do surface model-version diffs for outputs and you can pin a version to route.

14:58 (wrap-up chatter)

15:10 Alex: recap of next steps: Alex will send pricing and POC scope; Priya sends sandbox links and sample schemas; Vecora to supply canonical prompts and success metrics; schedule kickoff. thanks all.

15:25 (end)

Notes on transcript quality: some proper nouns mis-transcribed (e.g., Redwood Dedicate), occasional filler, timestamps approximate.
